note: Qatar: the other GCC states' citizens move freely; nationals of the countries listed get a free tourist visa on arrival for 90 or 30 days (some, as Indians and Pakistanis, only with a hotel booked through Discover Qatar: not modelled), and those of Belarus, Iran, Macao, Mauritius, Montenegro, Taiwan and others a paid one for 30 days. Everyone else may get a Hayya e-Visa online. Read from Wikipedia's copy of the Ministry of Interior's lists. Checked on 2026-11-03 against Qatar Tourism's own visa page (the state's tourism authority, citing the Ministry of Interior): it gives the GCC's free movement, visa-free entry for 102 nationalities, and a fee list (a paid visa on arrival, or a tourist visa beforehand on Hayya, QAR 100) that names Belarus, Iran, Macao, Mauritius, Montenegro, Taiwan, the Vatican and Serbia. Serbia, which Wikipedia's copy gave a free 90 days, is on the fee list, so it was moved to the paid 30 days. The page gives no length but the United States' (90 days a stay); the lengths, and the line between the paid visa on arrival and the e-Visa for everyone else, which the page blurs, stand on Wikipedia's copy of the Ministry's lists.

sources.title: Wikipedia, Visa policy of Qatar
sources.said: Citizens of the following Gulf Cooperation Council countries enjoy freedom of movement in Qatar. They do not require a visa under any circumstances, and are permitted to use a national ID card in lieu of a passport to enter Qatar: Bahrain Kuwait Oman Saudi Arabia United Arab Emirates ... Citizens of the following countries may obtain a free tourist visa on arrival for stays up to the duration listed below. However, some nationalities must meet additional criteria in order to be granted a free tourist visa on arrival: 90 days European Union member states (except Ireland) Antigua and Barbuda Argentina Armenia Bahamas Brazil Dominican Republic Iceland Liechtenstein Malaysia Norway Russia Serbia Seychelles South Korea Switzerland Turkey Ukraine United States 30 days Andorra Australia Azerbaijan Bolivia Bosnia and Herzegovina Brunei Canada Chile China Colombia Costa Rica Cuba Ecuador Georgia Guyana Hong Kong India Indonesia Ireland Japan Kazakhstan Lebanon Maldives Mexico Moldova Monaco New Zealand North Macedonia Pakistan Panama Paraguay Peru Rwanda San Marino Singapore South Africa Suriname Thailand United Kingdom Uruguay Uzbekistan Vatican City Venezuela ... 30 days Belarus Falkland Islands French Guiana Iran Macau Mauritius Montenegro Taiwan ... sources.title: Qatar Tourism (the state tourism authority), Visas
sources.said: Visit Qatar hassle-free with a visa-free entry to 102 nationalities & easy e-visa solution for the rest. ... Enter visa-free as GCC citizen. ... U.S citizens will receive a visa valid for two years, or until the passport expires, whichever comes first enabling multiple entries, with each stay up to 90 days. ... Visa-free entry is now the new term defining previously “visa on arrival”. Nothing changed except the name. Qatar-Oman Joint Tourist Visa This visa is issued upon arrival and is valid for 30 days ... Citizens of the following countries are eligible for the joint visa: Andorra, Australia, Austria, Belgium, Brunei, Canada, ... United Kingdom, United States, Vatican City ... The Qatar tourist visa is available to nationals of all countries, except GCC citizens, but citizens of over 102 countries are eligible for a free visa on arrival (see Visa-free entry above). Travellers of select nationalities will be required to pay a fee to obtain a visa on arrival or apply for a tourist visa prior to travel. Visas can be applied for on the Hayya platform for a cost of QAR 100. Afghanistan, Åland Islands, Albania, Algeria, ... Belarus, ... Holy See (the), ... Iran, ... Macao, ... Mauritius, ...
